import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Map 'is_fraud' numerical values to descriptive labels for better readability in plots
df['fraud_status'] = df['is_fraud'].map({0: 'Non-Fraud', 1: 'Fraud'})

# Set a professional style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(20, 6)) # 1 row, 3 columns for subplots

# Plot 1: Distribution of transaction amount by fraud status
sns.kdeplot(data=df, x='amount', hue='fraud_status', fill=True, common_norm=False, ax=axes[0])
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Amount')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Density')
axes[0].legend(title='Fraud Status')

# Plot 2: Distribution of transaction hour of day by fraud status
sns.kdeplot(data=df, x='hour_of_day', hue='fraud_status', fill=True, common_norm=False, ax=axes[1])
axes[1].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Hour by Fraud Status')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Density')
axes[1].set_xticks(range(0, 24, 2)) # Set ticks for every 2 hours for better readability
axes[1].legend(title='Fraud Status')

# Plot 3: Count of transaction types by fraud status
sns.countplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', hue='fraud_status', ax=axes[2])
axes[2].set_title('Transaction Type Counts by Fraud Status')
axes[2].set_xlabel('Transaction Type')
axes[2].set_ylabel('Count')
axes[2].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=15) # Rotate x-axis labels if they overlap
axes[2].legend(title='Fraud Status')

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping titles/labels
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
